title: Osibisa - Wikipedia
notes: In Ghana in the 1950s Teddy Osei, Sol Amarfio and others played in the highlife band the Star Gazers, then formed the Comets with Mac Tontoh, who had a West African hit with "(I Feel) Pata Pata" in 1958. Osei persuaded Amarfio and Tontoh to join him in London in 1969, and Osibisa was born, with Wendell Richardson, Lasisi Amao, Spartacus R and Robert Bailey: the "Beautiful Seven" of the first three albums. Style: "rock, progressive rock, acid rock, Latin, jazz, afro-funk, jazz fusion, soul, highlife, reggae, calypso and pop", classified as Afro-rock. Singles: "Sunshine Day" 1975 (UK No. 17, January 1976), "Dance the Body Music" 1976 (UK No. 31).

title: Sol Amarfio, a founding member of the Osibisa band has died (Gifty Owusu-Amoah, Graphic Online, 14 December 2022)
notes: Self-taught; nicknamed "The Rhythm Man" as a teenager. Played with the Rhythm Aces, the Star Gazers and the Comets in Ghana, moved to England in 1961 by way of Liberia, Spain and France, and worked with George Lee and Willie Cheetham in Europe and North Africa before Osibisa. From a 2018 Graphic Showbiz interview: "I do what comes naturally to me behind the drums. I don't force out anything"; he grew up with music and dance around him, and "the swing of those things sipped into me".

title: A big drum is broken - Tributes pour in for Sol Amarfo (Gifty Owusu-Amoah, Graphic Online, 15 December 2022)
notes: Musicians' tributes: "Sol was always so cool about his playing style that he made it seem effortless", "the beats were richly complex" (Kwesi Owusu); "I right away fell in love with Sol's drumming, especially on the Ayekoo Bia piece" (Nii Odoi Oddoye); the drummer Nii Tettey Tetteh decided to go professional after seeing Amarfio's success.

title: Osibisa - Phallus C (1971), Beat-Club, Radio Bremen (YouTube xEYPs3nbNJQ, the Beat-Club channel)
notes: The caption lists "Sol Amarfio dr". Looked at frame by frame: Amarfio at a kit wrapped in a black pearl, chrome hardware, brass cymbals, beside a painted Ghanaian drum; an ochre knitted cap, a white sleeveless smock with thin dark red stripes, a long chain with a pendant; matched grip, the sticks lifted high, full strokes from the arm.

title: Welcome Home (Osibisa album) - Wikipedia
notes: Island ILPS 9355, 1975, recorded at the Roundhouse, London, produced by Gerry Bron. Track 1, "Sunshine Day" (Amarfio, Osei, Tontoh), 4:59. Personnel: Sol Amarfio, drums, percussion, bells, bongos, congas; Kofi Ayivor, congas, percussion. "Dance the Body Music" is not on it.

title: Ojah Awake - Wikipedia
notes: Island ILPS 9411, 1976, recorded at the Roundhouse, produced by Gerry Bron. Track 1 "The Coffee Song", track 5 "Dance the Body Music" (Amarfio, Gyan, Osei, Tontoh), 3:56. Personnel: Sol Amarfio, drums, percussion, cowbells, bongos; Kofi Ayivor, congas, percussion.

title: Woyaya (album) - Wikipedia
notes: MCA, 1971, produced by Tony Visconti at AIR Studios. "Woyaya" written by Amarfio. Personnel: Sol Amarfio, drums, fontomfrom, bongos, African drums, cowbells, percussion, vocals.

title: Heads (Osibisa album) - Wikipedia
notes: MCA, 1972. "Che Che Kule" written by Amarfio. Personnel: Sol Amarfio, African drums, bells, bongos, cowbells, drums, percussion, vocals.
